title: Team Lab: Put Your Own Agent on the Flywheel
html:
Goal: as a team, pick a scenario close to your business, give every member one role, and take one full turn of the six stages — from signing the first criteria version to admitting the first production feedback and signing the second version — then show your evidence to the room in 15 minutes.

Prerequisites

  • At least one team member has walked the whole main line (the Define chapter to the Improve chapter) and knows where every sign-off button is.
  • The team has a host console and everyone has their account, per Teams and Roles; the business owner and release operator hold their permissions.
  • The host console's workspace default already has release policy gated (Roles and Separation of Duties).

Use fictional data only. Never put a real customer, a real company name, real orders or any personal data (names, ID numbers, phone numbers, addresses) into prompts, knowledge base documents, golden sets or chats. Reuse "Unicorn Company" or invent a fictional brand for your scenario.

1. Pick a scenario (planned: 15 minutes)

Industry Example scenarios
Retail In-store shopping assistant, stock and replenishment Q&A, membership benefits
E-commerce Pre-sale product recommendation, order and shipping lookup, returns, merchant operations assistant
OTA Trip planning, bundled product recommendation, corporate travel approval and booking
Flights Flight search and fare comparison, change/refund fee calculation, baggage and special services, schedule-change notices
Hotels Room recommendation, booking and cancellation policy Q&A, pre- and post-stay service, review summaries

You can also bring an agent prototype you are already working on, migrate it to AgentCore with BYOC or Strands Agents, and take it through all six stages (see the end of section 2).

Once chosen, spend 10 minutes on a scenario card — it is the input to every later stage:

text
Scenario:
Target users: (who asks, and when?)
Three most typical tasks:
  1.
  2.
  3.
Red lines (at least one; decidable by code, trajectory or metric — not by an LLM score):
Policy document: (1–2 pages of fictional policy with rule ids and at least one worked calculation)
Ready-to-ship bar: (one sentence per dimension, written like "Quality: fee calculations correct in at least 90% of cases")

Here is a filled-in example (a hotel cancellation scenario, based on the Unicorn Hotels policy from the Build chapter); write yours at this level of detail:

text
Scenario: Unicorn Hotels cancellation assistant
Target users: guests who booked a Unicorn Hotels room through Unicorn Trip and, a few days before arrival, change plans and ask "how much is charged if I cancel now?"
Three most typical tasks:
  1. Decide whether now is still inside the free-cancellation window (Flexible H-02, Standard Prepaid H-03, the 72-hour National Day rule H-09)
  2. Work out what is charged and what is refunded (the H-10 worked example: Standard Prepaid ¥680/night × 3 nights, cancelled less than 48 hours before check-in: first night ¥680 charged, ¥1,360 refunded)
  3. Explain the exceptions and what cannot be cancelled (Non-refundable Saver H-04 and its flight-cancellation exception; groups of 10 or more rooms go to a human, H-12)
Red lines (at least one; decidable by code, trajectory or metric — not by an LLM score):
  P1 The agent answers within 120 seconds (P95) — metric Latency P95 (ms), threshold 120000
Policy document: unicorn-hotels-cancellation.en.md (H-01 to H-12; H-10 is the worked example)
Ready-to-ship bar:
  Performance: P95 latency at most 30 seconds
  Cost: at most 2000 tokens per session (set from your cost budget)
  Cognition: free-or-not and which rule applies match the expected answer in at least 80% of cases
  Quality: the amounts charged and refunded are correct in at least 90% of cases
  Responsibility: no promise of a free cancellation or refund the policy does not allow (including the Non-refundable Saver, H-04) in at least 95% of cases

Every rule id and amount in the example comes from unicorn-hotels-cancellation.en.md (H-02, H-03, H-04, H-09, H-10, H-12). The red line P1 is the same row as P1 in the main-line criteria table: executor Metric, metric Latency P95 (ms), <= 120000. The criteria table refuses only a red line decided by an LLM judge (criteria.redline_judge); a metric, a code assertion or a trajectory matcher can all carry a red line.

For the policy document and the golden set, use the main-track files as templates:

  • Policy documents: the three policies from section 4.1 of the Build chapter, ecommerce-returns-policy.en.md, unicorn-air-change-refund-baggage.en.md and unicorn-hotels-cancellation.en.md — one id per rule, amounts and time limits written out, a worked calculation at the end.
  • Golden set: follow the structure explained in section 3 of Phase 1 · Define, using unicorn-service-golden.en.json as the template — one object per item: scenario_id, turns[0].input (the user's question), turns[0].expected_response (the expected answer, written by a person), metadata.dlc.case_tier (known_good / known_bad / ambiguous / adversarial), metadata.dlc.criteria_ids, metadata.dlc.origin (manual), metadata.dlc.expected_source (annotator) and metadata.policy_refs (shaped like ["H-03", "H-10"]); the template also carries an optional metadata.line (business line). A scenario_id cannot repeat within a split (golden.duplicate_scenario), and case_tier must be one of the four values above (golden.bad_case_tier). When the splits are curated in one call, items without a top-level split field are stratified by case tier and divided 50% / 30% / 20% into dev, regression and holdout.

2. One turn of the flywheel: what each stage delivers (planned: 3 hours)

Stage Done by Deliverable (have it ready for the demo) Planned time Reference
Define Developer drafts, business owner signs Criteria v1 covering all five dimensions (a dimension that does not apply gets n/a:<dimension> <reason> in a criterion note), at least one red line, signed by the business owner; golden set of ≥ 15 items, three splits curated, holdout sealed 40 min The Define chapter
Build Developer Deployed agent (Strands ZIP or managed Harness recommended) with the policy knowledge base; at least three tasks work in the Chat Playground 40 min The Build chapter
Evaluate Developer runs; developer + domain expert annotate; business owner decides A release evaluation report (verdict one of PASS / BLOCKED / INVALID) and a cost estimate; at least one judge criterion calibrated (two annotators, decider is not an annotator) 40 min The Evaluate chapter
Release Developer requests, release ops signs live points at the signed version; any waiver has a reason, a risk owner and an expiry 20 min The Release chapter
Observe Whole team ≥ 10 sessions of traffic; a waterfall analysis of one trace (where the time and tokens went); drift watch scheduled and run once 20 min The Observe chapter
Improve Domain expert corrects, business owner admits, developer drafts v2 ≥ 1 production candidate admitted to regression with a human-written expected answer, duplicates rejected with a reason; one regression run; criteria v2 signed; a fix-ladder screenshot 40 min The Improve chapter

Key points and pitfalls per stage:

  • Define: write each criterion with the agent as subject and an observable predicate; cost and performance can only be metrics (latency_p95_ms, cost_per_success_usd, tokens_per_session); a red line cannot be decided by an LLM judge; gate thresholds lie in (0, 100%]. A judge criterion is only observed until calibrated — do not count on an uncalibrated gate to stop a bad version. Expected answers in the golden set are written by people, and do not make every case tier Known good. To curate the three splits, pick your golden-set JSON file with the file button in the Curate the splits dialog, as in section 4 of the Evaluate chapter: give every item its own metadata.dlc.case_tier and criteria_ids, and the dialog keeps them; the holdout can be curated only once.
  • Build: give the knowledge base documents rule ids so answers can cite them. In gated mode every deploy lands on candidate; live moves only after sign-off.
  • Evaluate: read the cost estimate before you start a run. The gate's evaluation runs invoke a fresh candidate endpoint themselves, so it needs no warm-up. Issuing an annotation link needs judge.calibrate; the issuer becomes an evidence author of that task and may no longer decide it (calibration.own_labels), so let admin issue the links and leave the decision to the business owner. If more than 5% of the denominator is undetermined the report is INVALID — fix the data or the evaluator rather than lowering the threshold.
  • Release: signing needs a PASS and signer ≠ requester; red lines are never waivable.
  • Observe: read the scorecard as the business owner; read spend and decision history as the administrator.
  • Improve: admission writes dev or regression only, never holdout; after publishing a new criteria version, Save the drift watch again so it uses the new version.

Optional: bring your own agent (BYOC). As developer, open Modules → Agent development → New agent (/v3/create) and, under Other ways to build on the right, click Bring your own code.

In the image: 1 Bring your own code under "Other ways to build".

Expected result: the page stays inside the V3 frame and opens V2's New agent wizard (address /v2/agents?view=new&method=byoc) directly on step 2, Configure; Code artifact has three cards: Code zip, Dockerfile build and Existing ECR image. Under Resource name it says "Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, 3–48 characters, starting with a letter — it can't change after creation." The full upload and deploy steps are option B in the Build chapter. A BYOC agent goes through criteria, golden set, release gate and observability like any other agent, but these depend on platform-generated code and are not available to it: mounting a managed knowledge base or registry skills (the Build chapter's capability table), config-bundle A/B experiments and canaries (backend/app/optimization/service.py answers custom-source-unverified for byoc), and Accept & publish new version (managed Harness only). The Build row above requires the policy knowledge base, so finish the main line with Strands ZIP or a managed Harness first and treat BYOC as a bonus. Also, a BYOC code zip only produces traces with the ADOT launcher: add aws-opentelemetry-distro to requirements.txt (and keep dependency installation on), or use a Dockerfile build started with opentelemetry-instrument; otherwise Observability cannot see it and evaluation reports that the agent produced no spans.

3. 15-minute demo template

One presenter per team; every other role demonstrates the step they signed (whoever signed it presents it).

Time (planned) Topic Show
0:00–2:00 Scenario and users The scenario card: target users, three tasks, red lines
2:00–4:00 The standard Criteria v1 (five dimensions, red lines, signer); golden-set splits and coverage
4:00–7:00 The evidence Release evaluation report and cost estimate; a judge calibration's κ and decider; release ops' sign-off
7:00–9:00 Production Observability dashboard, one trace waterfall analysis, the drift watch alerts card
9:00–12:00 Improve One bad answer from thumbs-down to admission; the v1 → v2 criteria diff; The agent got better by / The standard got harder by on the fix ladder
12:00–13:00 Decision history The administrator's view: who signed, who admitted, who released (golden.admit, criteria.sign, release.sign). The Standards → Decision history page only shows records whose target contains the selected agent's ID; the targets of these three are the candidate, the criteria-set version and the release record IDs, so they never appear on that page — show them as admin from <ConsoleUrl>/api/audit?action=golden.admit (likewise criteria.sign, release.sign); the browser shows the raw JSON, field events
13:00–15:00 Retrospective and questions What you would change next round: the agent, the standard, or the data

4. Scoring rubric (100 points)

Dimension Points What full marks look like
Quality of the standard 20 Criteria have the agent as subject and are observable; every dimension has a criterion or a written n/a; red lines are deterministic; thresholds have a business reason
Quality of the golden set 15 Expected answers written by people; sensible case-tier mix (known bad, ambiguous or adversarial included); holdout sealed and never written by admission
Evidence and separation of duties 20 Drafting, signing, annotating, deciding calibration and signing the release were done by different people, provable from the decision history
Evaluation and release 15 A cost estimate exists; the gate verdict is PASS, or a BLOCKED was correctly stopped and explained (an INVALID needs its evidence completed and a re-run first)
Observability 10 One real trace explains where latency and tokens went; drift watch scheduled
Closing the loop 15 At least one production candidate entered regression with a human-written expected answer; criteria v2 signed; the team can read both fix-ladder numbers
Demo 5 Done within 15 minutes; each role presents the step they signed

Bonus (up to +10): a BYOC agent; one A/B experiment or canary; a recommendation fixed and shipped, visible as Fixed on the fix ladder.

5. Wrap-up

After the demos, follow the Cleanup chapter. Extra steps for the team lab:

  • For every team agent: developer opens Modules → Agent evaluation → Standards, picks the team agent in the header, switches to the Drift watch tab, unchecks Enabled in the Schedule card and clicks Save.
  • developer opens Modules → Agent evaluation → Online evaluation (/v3/online) and clicks the Pause or Delete icon button at the right of the team's config row (hover shows the name). Pause opens the Pause online evaluation dialog ("Stop judging new sessions for <config name>? Existing results are kept."); click Pause, and the row turns Paused with a Start icon in place of Pause (frontend/src/v3/pages/Online.tsx). Delete opens the Delete online evaluation dialog ("Delete <config name>? The results log group /aws/bedrock-agentcore/evaluations/results/<config name>-… is kept."); click Delete.
  • biz-owner (the account that created the reviewer links in the Improve chapter) opens Modules → Agent runtime → Issue box, clicks Reviewers at the right of the page header, picks the team agent in the drop-down, clicks Revoke on every row whose state is Active in the Reviewer links table, and clicks Revoke in the "Revoke this link?" dialog ("The reviewer loses access immediately. Their earlier ratings are kept."). Expected result: the row's state becomes Revoked and its Revoke button is greyed out. A link can be revoked, not deleted.

In the image: 1 Reviewers at the right of the Issue box header; 2 Revoke on the active link's row; 3 Revoke in the "Revoke this link?" dialog.

  • admin opens Modules → Configuration → User Management (/v3/users), clicks Disable on each self-registered team account's row, and clicks Disable in the Disable account dialog ("Disable <username>? The account loses console access immediately; you can enable it again later."). Expected result: Status becomes Disabled and the row button changes to Enable. To remove the account entirely, click the row's Delete icon button and click Delete in the Delete account dialog ("Delete <username>? The account loses console access immediately."); the row disappears from the list.

In the image: 1 Disable on the account's row; 2 Disable in the Disable account dialog.

Checklist

  • Every role is held by a different member on their own account; business owner and release ops have their permissions
  • Criteria v1 signed; golden set curated into three splits with holdout sealed
  • The agent passed the release gate and live points at the signed version
  • At least 10 sessions of traffic; the drift watch has run once
  • At least one production candidate admitted to regression; criteria v2 signed; both fix-ladder numbers readable
  • The 15-minute demo is done and the decision history proves who performed every sign-off

Troubleshooting

Symptom Cause Fix
Signing fails with criteria.self_sign The signer created or last edited this version (administrators excepted) Have a member who neither created nor edited this version sign
Creating an annotation task fails with annotation.annotators Fewer than two annotators Tick at least two annotators
A calibration decision fails with calibration.own_labels The decider is an annotator, the adjudicator or an annotation-link issuer of that task The business owner, who neither annotated nor issued a link, decides
Deciding "aligned" fails with calibration.not_supported Judge–human agreement (κ) is below the floor Record "not aligned", improve the criterion and label another round
A release sign-off is refused The verdict is not PASS, or the signer is the requester Fix it to PASS first; release ops signs
Teams overwrite each other's resources Shared console without a team prefix Prefix agents, knowledge bases, criteria tables and golden sets with t<team>- (an agent resource name allows only lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, 3–48 characters, starting with a letter); custom evaluator and online-evaluation config names allow only letters, digits and underscores (up to 48), so prefix them with t<team>_
